First floor spaces include property management and resident services offices, a large community room for use by residents and community groups, a religious facility and ancillary space. Level 0 uses include structured parking, and a food bank. Parking for approximately 84 vehicles is proposed: approximately 72 spaces within the building structure and 12 surface parking spaces are proposed. Tree Solutions Inc. (TSI) assessed 56 trees in the Salishan neighborhood for tree root and sidewalk 
conflicts. The sidewalks were heaving, lifting at seams, and cracking in several places with tripping 
hazards of up to one to three inches in some locations.  
 
The trees were likely planted in the early 2000s when Salishan neighborhood was redeveloped. It 
appears that the trees were planted in shallow heavily compacted soil, which can lead to the 
development of surface roots exacerbating tree root and sidewalk conflicts. In addition, these conditions 
can limit access to water and oxygen leading to health decline, which was evident in several of the trees 
we assessed.  
 
There were four trees with conflicts severe enough warrant removal. Management of the remaining 
trees should be evaluated based on the species and health of the tree, the cost of the potential work, 
and the condition sidewalk conflicts of neighboring trees. We recommend either retaining and 
monitoring or removing and replacing 16 of the green ash (Fraxinus pennsylvanica) trees, which are 
susceptible to an emerging insect pest called Emerald Ash Borer, were in poor to fair health condition, 
and although sidewalk repairs may be possible, the longevity of the tree may not warrant the 
investment in managing these trees. We recommend evaluating the possibility of repairing sidewalks 
around eleven trees which may need grade changes to accommodate a repair. The remaining trees all 
appeared to be able to be retained with repairs to the sidewalk and improvements to the site 
conditions. Further details can be found in the attached tables and in the body of the report.
